correctness.rationale: Direct Binet analysis proves the Zeckendorf digit-deletion map and last-bit threshold. The predecessor difference formula and strict bounds establish backward closure of the admissible window for all valid pairs. Density of the irrational rotation yields every open cell; each distinct cell has a distinct bit/difference tuple. A count of the integer and theta-shifted breakpoint lattices gives 2m+2 minus four explicit indicator corrections and total 6m²+6m−4, including m=1 collisions. Standard transition invariance and known absorbing-window inequalities preserve recognition. Standalone integer BFS checks every multiplier 1..60, with an independent numeral-pair enumeration for 1..12; these tests supplement but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 Moradi–Rampersad–Shallit paper and Moradi thesis construct the exact four-coordinate multiplier automaton and bound its ambient state count by 36m². They do not calculate its exact reachable subset; the thesis explicitly identifies understanding reachable states as future work. This theorem gives the sharp reachable-state polynomial and every difference-coordinate fiber. Direct two-track minimum-state tables and older one-track divisibility results do not imply the formula. Focused published and mathematical-record searches found no covering result, with residual unindexed-work risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed literature may contain an equivalent exact reachability formula.
This is an exact reachable-subgraph theorem, not a minimum-DFA theorem; it does not resolve the unknown asymptotically sharp minimal-state formula.

value.rationale: The motivating authors explicitly identify the reachable part of their arithmetic automaton as a mathematical object needing better understanding. The result gives a complete exact census for every multiplier, sharp per-difference fibers and a factor-six improvement on the ambient constructive quadratic state bound. Its elementary irrational-rotation geometry explains an otherwise opaque exceptional constant; neither a routine numeric lookup nor a restatement of minimal DFA tables. The scope distinction is preserved.
